carousels.caption: Gmail’s spam filter ignores your subject line—it’s all about sender reputation. Fix these 6 settings to land in the inbox every time. #emailmarketingtips #emaildeliverability #marketingaudit #smallbusiness
carousels.hook: Gmail’s spam filter ignores your subject line—it’s all about sender trust
carousels.throughline: Gmail’s spam filter prioritizes sender reputation and engagement over subject lines—here’s how to adjust your settings to land in the inbox.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail buries your emails before reading the subject—it’s all about sender trust

body.text: Gmail checks your domain’s sending history first, so new senders start in spam.
It looks for replies and forwards to decide if your emails are wanted, not just opened.
Missing an easy unsubscribe link can get your emails flagged as spam instantly.
Use a warm-up tool like Mailflow to build trust with Gmail’s system over time.

carousels.hook: Gmail flags ‘free’ and ‘discount’ as spam—here’s what works instead
carousels.throughline: Gmail’s spam filter skips common trigger words—here’s what to use instead for better deliverability.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail buries your emails if the subject says ‘free’ or ‘discount’—here’s what works instead

body.text: Gmail flags ‘free,’ ‘discount,’ and ‘urgent’ as spam triggers instantly—avoid them.
Personalized subject lines with names or locations perform 22% better than generic ones.
Questions in subject lines get opened 30% more than statements—try one today.
Gmail’s filter checks for natural language, not just keywords—keep it conversational.
